newsitem.title: GERMANY: UAL corrects statement on Boeing.
newsitem.headline: UAL corrects statement on Boeing.

text.p: United Airlines, the U.S. carrier, said on Friday that it has ordered seven additional airplanes from European manufacturer Airbus and was also negotiating with Boeing about three more planes.
The statement corrects an earlier press release from UAL issued in Bonn which contained a translation error that said UAL had cancelled an order to Boeing.
Last August, United Airlines placed large plane orders with Airbus and Boeing as part of a fleet modernisation.
UAL said it would add four Airbus 319 and three Airbus 320 planes to an order for 24 A319s placed in August.
"United Airlines is in negotiations with Boeing concerning three additional jumbo jets," the company said in its corrected statement.
UAL said that the orders were part of a general modernisation of its carrier fleet for which it would invest some $5.2 billion to the year 2000 and retire 111 aging aircraft.
